title: Ratio & Proportion
description: Simplifying ratios, dividing quantities, direct and inverse proportion, and real-world applications.

notes.heading: Simplifying Ratios
notes.body: A ratio compares quantities. Simplify by dividing all parts by their HCF. Example: 12:18 → HCF=6 → 2:3. To divide a quantity in a ratio, add the parts to find total shares, divide by total, then multiply each part.

notes.heading: Direct and Inverse Proportion
notes.body: Direct proportion: y=kx (both increase together). Example: 5 pens cost £2.50 → 8 pens = (2.50÷5)×8 = £4.00. Inverse proportion: y=k/x (one increases as other decreases). Example: 4 workers take 6 days → 8 workers take 3 days.

notes.heading: Map Scales and Best Value
notes.body: Map scale 1:50000 means 1cm = 500m. Best value: compare unit price (cost per gram or per item). Example: 400g for £1.60 = 0.4p/g; 600g for £2.10 = 0.35p/g → larger pack is better value.
